purpose: Tinidazole is used to treat certain infections caused by bacteria or tiny parasites called protozoa. It is commonly prescribed for infections like bacterial vaginosis, trichomoniasis (a sexually transmitted infection), and intestinal infections caused by parasites such as Giardia or amoeba. Your doctor prescribed it to help clear up one of these types of infections.
how_it_works: Tinidazole works by entering the bacteria or parasite and damaging their DNA, which stops them from being able to grow and reproduce. Think of it like cutting the power supply to the germ so it cannot survive or spread. Over time, this kills off the infection in your body.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, stomach upset, vomiting, a bitter or metallic taste in your mouth, loss of appetite, and diarrhea. Some people may also feel dizzy or get a headache. These effects are usually mild and go away after you finish the medication.
warnings: Do not drink any alcohol while taking tinidazole and for at least 3 days after your last dose — this can cause a severe reaction including flushing, nausea, vomiting, and rapid heartbeat. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as this medication may not be safe. Also let your doctor know about all other medications you take, as tinidazole can interact with blood thinners like warfarin. Avoid it if you have had a bad reaction to similar medications like metronidazole (Flagyl).
typical_dosing: Tinidazole is usually taken as a single large dose or once daily for 2 to 5 days depending on the type of infection being treated. It is best taken with food to reduce stomach upset. Always take the full prescribed course even if you feel better early.
